subject: CloudWave integration: SDK options, auth, routing & tool-call patterns
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Sophie Turner <sophie@cloudwave.io>, Alex Reed <alex.reed@cloudwave.io>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>, Tessa Morgan <tessa@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 10 Jun 2026 14:02:00 -0700
Subject: CloudWave call recap + integration options (SDK, auth, routing, tools)

Hi Sophie / Alex — thanks again for the time today. Quick recap from our discovery and proposed next steps so we keep momentum. Notes below are intentionally tactical so your engineering team can react.

High-level ask you mentioned:
- Integrate LLM-based routing + re-ranker into CloudWave’s existing request pipeline for public docs search and customer-support triage.
- Need on-prem ingestion for attachments and a secure embeddings store (KMS-backed).
- Expect ~80 QPS peak for search rerank, burst to 200 QPS during peak campaigns.

Recommendations and architecture options (short):
1) SDK + Auth patterns
   - Option A: Lightweight Redwood SDK embedded in your backend (recommended for fastest time-to-prod). Uses API key + mTLS to our hosted control plane; KMS integration for embedding keys.
   - Option B: Private deployment (VPC) with customer-managed control plane. We surface the same SDK surface but auth is IAM-backed (SAML/OAuth) and keys live in your KMS/HSM.
   - Tradeoffs: A faster to ship; B required if compliance prevents tokens leaving your VPC.

2) Routing + model selection
   - Edge routing layer in your service: call SDK's router with request metadata (region, latency SLO, tenancy). Router returns selected model variant and fallback policy.
   - For search rerank, we recommend a two-stage call: embeddings->ANN search (your infra) -> ranking request to Redwood with top-N context. This keeps token costs down and preserves latency.

3) Tool/Function calling patterns (key part of today’s ask)
   - Tool definitions: create small, idempotent tool endpoints (PDF_extractor, DB_lookup, Ticket_create). Each tool has a concise schema for inputs/outputs and an error contract (HTTP 4xx for client errors, 5xx for infra).
   - Tool choice strategy: prefer deterministic tools for retrieval (embeddings+ANN) and generative tools for synthesis only.
   - Parallel tools: run non-dependent tools in parallel (e.g., PDF_extractor + Metadata_fetch) and aggregate results before the model call. Use a scatter-gather pattern with time budget.
   - Error handling: model receives standardized tool response objects and a status field. On transient failure, retry tool once with exponential backoff; if still failing, populate model-visible fallback text and surface telemetry to Redwood Console.

4) Structured output & reranker integration
   - Use structured JSON output schema for the model to emit (items: {doc_id, score, snippet, rationale}) to avoid brittle parsing.
   - For reranker, Redwood returns both token-level explanation and calibrated score; keep your business logic to re-weight based on recency or SLA tags.

Next steps I propose:
- I’ll drop a short mutual action plan (MAP) with milestones and owners (attached).
- Laura: can you draft an initial SDK integration snippet + sample tool definition for their PDF_extractor?
- Priyom: please assemble a quick capacity/latency config proposal (suggested: dedicated pool with burst to shared for campaign windows).
- Sophie / Alex: a 30-45 minute follow-up this week focused on network/auth constraints and a quick look at their internal ANN layer.

Attachments: CloudWave_Redwood_MAP_v1.pdf (MAP), redwood_proposed_config.yaml (capacity sketch)

Thanks —
Karthik Iyer
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
karthik@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0110

From: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
To: Sophie Turner <sophie@cloudwave.io>, Alex Reed <alex.reed@cloudwave.io>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 10 Jun 2026 16:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: CloudWave call recap + integration options (SDK, auth, routing, tools)

Sophie / Alex — following up with the technical sketch I promised. Paste below is a compact example for SDK usage + tool definition to show how we recommend modelling the PDF_extractor and the parallel pattern.

1) SDK snippet (pseudo-JS)
const redwood = new Redwood({ auth: { type: 'api_key', key: process.env.RW_API_KEY }, region: 'us-west' });

// Parallel tool calls (scatter-gather)
const [pdfResult, metaResult] = await Promise.all([
  fetch('https://files.cloudwave.io/extract?fileId=123'),
  fetch('https://meta.cloudwave.io/manifest?id=123')
]);
const toolInputs = { pdf: await pdfResult.json(), meta: await metaResult.json() };

const response = await redwood.callModel('reranker-v1', {
  input: { query, topDocs, toolOutputs: toolInputs },
  structuredSchema: 'cloudwave_rerank_v1'
});

2) Tool definition (OpenAPI-like short form)
- name: PDF_Extractor
  endpoint: https://files.cloudwave.io/extract
  method: POST
  input_schema: { fileId: 'string' }
  output_schema: { text: 'string', pages: 'int', embeddings_ref: 'string' }
  error_contract: { code: 'int', message: 'string', transient: 'bool' }

3) Auth notes
- For hosted: API keys scoped per-project + mTLS optional. Store keys in your KMS and rotate monthly.
- For private VPC: we recommend IAM + short-lived tokens minted by your identity provider. SDK supports a token provider hook so you can inject credentials at runtime.

4) Edge routing example
- Request enters your API gateway -> tag request (region, org_tier) -> call Redwood SDK route() -> returns modelVariant and endpoint. SDK handles connection pooling and KV cache hints.

5) Failure modes and observability hooks
- Add correlation_id to all tool calls. If a tool fails, the model will receive {status: 'tool_error', code: 502, message: '...'} and you can map to a fallback flow.
- Push tool telemetry to Redwood Console via the SDK telemetry endpoint; set sample rate to 10% to start.

I attached a minimal OpenAPI YAML for PDF_Extractor and a proposed structured schema (see redwood_proposed_config.yaml). Happy to walk through these in the follow-up with Alex.

Cheers,
Laura Bennett
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
laura@redwood.com

From: Alex Reed <alex.reed@cloudwave.io>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
Cc: Sophie Turner <sophie@cloudwave.io>
Date: Thu, 11 Jun 2026 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: CloudWave call recap + integration options (SDK, auth, routing, tools)

Thanks Karthik/Laura — this is very helpful. A few clarifying items from our side after an internal quick sync: 
- Compliance: we must keep embeddings encrypted in our HSM; public API keys are a no-go. Private VPC option is preferred.
- ANN layer: we run FAISS in a k8s cluster and can return top-50 in <40ms. We'll push top-10 to Redwood for reranking.
- Parallelism: we like the scatter-gather idea but need guidance on time budgets — what do you recommend for a 150ms target latency for rerank?

Action items on us:
- We will share example ANN outputs and a sample doc corpus for embedding tests (you can use a temporary sandbox).
- Sophie will coordinate an internal network review for VPC peering.

Could we schedule the tech follow-up tomorrow morning?

—Alex

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Sophie Turner <sophie@cloudwave.io>, Alex Reed <alex.reed@cloudwave.io>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>, Tessa Morgan <tessa@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 11 Jun 2026 09:17:00 -0700
Subject: Re: CloudWave call recap + integration options (SDK, auth, routing, tools)

Perfect — thanks Alex. Quick replies to the questions and proposed times: 
- Latency guidance: for a 150ms tail we recommend: ANN top-50 in <50ms, parallel tool extraction <40ms (run async), model rerank window target 40-60ms on a dedicated pool. That implies end-to-end P95 ~140ms with small buffer. We'll include concrete pool sizing in Priyom's config doc.
- For HSM + VPC: we will provision a Private deployment trial (30 days) and provide an IAM integration guide. Laura, Priyom — can you own setup checklist?
- Time: Tomorrow 9:30–10:00 PT works for our team — send invite and agenda.

Attached: CloudWave_Redwood_MAP_v1.pdf (walks through milestones)

Karthik
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
karthik@redwood.com
